newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says Israeli agents kill nine in bus bombing.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israeli agents kill nine in bus bombing.

text.p: Syria accused on Thursday Israeli agents of bombing a bus in central Damascus on Tuesday, killing nine people and wounding 44.
Israel denied the charge and the United States said it could not confirm that Israeli agents were responsible and warned Damascus against making "wild and irresponsible" statements.
A Syrian spokesman hinted in a statement to the official Syrian news agency SANA that the incident was linked to recent attacks against Syrian interests in Lebanon.
"Nine people were killed and 44 others were wounded in the criminal action against a transport bus in Damascus," he said.
"This terrorist, cowardly and criminal action comes within the framework of threats which were launched recently by Israeli officials that aim at killing the (Middle East) peace process."

"Agents of the (Israeli intelligence agency) Mossad utilised preparations for the New Year celebrations on Tuesday 31.12.1996 with people leaving to their towns and planted an explosive device inside the bus which exploded minutes after it left the bus station at noon," the official said.
In Jerusalem, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak told Reuters: "It's a gross lie. Israel strives for nothing but peace and acts solely in peaceful ways."
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns described the Syrian charge as very serious and urged Damascus to give evidence before making the accusation.

"It is a very serious charge for one state to accuse another of actually sponsoring bombings in its capital...If the Syrian government and the Syrian press cannot back up what they are saying, well they ought not to make that charge. It's a wild and irresponsible charge if in fact it is not backed up by evidence," Burns said.
Witnesses in the Syrian capital said the bus exploded just metres away from the station of luxurious buses in central Damascus which was filled with New Year's eve shoppers.

"Several passers by were wounded in the 1.30 p.m. (1130 gmt) blast which also smashed small shops in the area," one witness said. "Luckily the university's hospital was close and many of the severly wounded were rushed to it for treatment.
"The interior minister inspected the scene minutes after the blast and the area was sealed off by security to allow ambulances to take away the injured," the official said.
The bus station, one of several used to carry passengers to various Syrian cities, is close to the handicraft centre and the military museum.
The Syrian official said that among the wounded was a family of 11.
He said the bus which was bombed used to travel on a route linking the north Syrian city of Aleppo with Beirut but it changed its route on New Year's eve to Damascus-Aleppo.
Diplomats said that revealing that the bus used to travel to Lebanon was a hint that the incident was connected to recent attacks against Syrian targets in neighbouring Lebanon.
Syria is the main foreign power broker in Lebanon where it has some 35,000 troops. Israel occupies a self-declared security zone in south Lebanon.

Last month there were one or two attacks on Syrian targets in Lebanon. Leaflets distributed in Beirut also condemned Syria's military presence in Lebanon and criticised the pro-Syrian Lebanese government.

The incidents -- also blamed by Lebanese and Syrian officials on Israeli agents -- included an attack with machineguns against Syrian workers driving in a bus in the mainly Christian area north of Beirut on December 19.
The driver of the bus was killed and some passengers were wounded in the attack.
"The Mossad agents wanted to kill innocent people with their ugly crime which is added to their records which are full of acts of organised terrorism...," the Syrian official said of Tuesday's blast.
Earlier a beirut-based businessman who has just returned from a trip to Damascus told Reuters in Nicosia, Cyprus, that 15 people were killed and 50 wounded in the explosion.
